The food was decent but the service was dreadful
Dec 2018 • Couples
The Tung Garden is a Chinese restaurant located in the Eastin Saigon hotel [which is relatively close to and convenient for Ho Chi Minh City airport (SGN)]. It is one of the two restaurants in the hotel, the other being a ‘western-style’ establishment. We chose the Tung Garden because the ambience and furnishings seemed preferable. My wife and I were transiting rapidly through SGN en route from Hanoi to the UK and this was to be our last evening in Vietnam. It was Boxing Day, i.e. the day after Christmas day. 

I don’t understand why hotels and restaurants the world over seem to think that ‘Christmas music’ should be played perpetually over the Christmas period. Some of it is decent (for example, ‘White Christmas’ sung by Bing Crosby) but, when one has heard so frequently in a short period of time, it does begin to pall. Other ‘Christmas music’ is simply trite (for example, ‘Little Drummer Boy’). The Tung Garden was still playing Christmas music on Boxing Day. Somebody must have forgotten to change the CD.

We arrived at about 20:00. The restaurant was deserted apart from the staff, though I think that another diner arrived later. As soon as we were seated, about 3 – 4 members of staff hovered around us to take our order. Now this could be viewed as being solicitous, but our cynical interpretation was that the staff just wanted us fed as quickly as possible so that they could go home. We tried to explain that we wanted a drink before ordering so that we could peruse the extensive menu. It was difficult to communicate this to the staff. Eventually, my bottle of beer arrived. The staff had a problem opening it. My wife’s gin and tonic eventually arrived – a part-filled tumbler of gin, an unopened tin of tonic and a glass with some ice in it! We assume that she was just supposed to prepare it herself. We’ve never encountered this before.
The staff were still hovering so I just bluntly told them to go way, which they eventually did. We made our choices – beef with noodles, deep fried prawns in soy sauce, sweet and sour pork and fried rice with pine nuts and ordered. Each dish was denoted by a number in the menu, so there should have been no confusion. We had expected that everything would arrive together. We were mistaken. The prawns arrived first, which was not too bad as they could be considered to be a starter, then the fried rice arrived. The waiter removed the cover from the dish, but we put the top back on as no further dishes appeared. We waited and waited but nothing else arrived. We had to ask what had happened to the rest of the dishes. ‘They are coming’ the waiter implied (the waiter spoke very little English, but this should not have really been a problem as sign language is perfectly effective). Eventually, the noodles arrived. We could not be bothered waiting for the sweet and sour pork, so we started eating. The final dish arrived, it was belly pork (which I loathe) with broccoli!. We sent it back, having pointed again to the sweet and sour pork in the menu. After we had finished the noodles and the rice, the sweet and sour pork arrived, but we had nothing to accompany it, so we sent it back (it did smell quite good.)

We decided that enough was enough and asked for the bill. There had been an automatic 5% service charge added, as is normal in Vietnam. I refused to pay this and I recalculated the bill without the service charge. This is the first time that I have EVER done this in many years of eating out. In summary, the service was execrable, which was a pity as the food was good and plentiful. It’s a shame that the last evening of our trip was such a disaster. Given the rest of the reviews, perhaps we visited the restaurant at the wrong time.

Good Peking Duck and service
Oct 2018 • Couples
I and my bf loves Peiking Duck and we like to explore new places for this. Today we found a 50% discount for Peiking Duck at Tung Garden and we gave it a try. It only cost 22 usd/whole duck, it was amazing deal and it was delicious, the duck’s skin was crispy wraped perfectly in thin crepe and serve with sweet bean sauce. The second dish is the duck meat with stir fried noodle, We was impressed by the tender of the roasted meat, combined well with thin egg noodle topped with onion and sprout. The downside is the restaurant atsmotsphere quite old fashioned eventhough it was placed in Eastin Hotel, but the service was good and definitely value for money.

Dinner !!! Chiness Food when in Ho Chi Minh
Dec 2017 • Family
This is a recommended place for Chinese Dinner, is not far from Airport in the Eastin Grand Hotel.
We are there to try the Roast piglet, Peking Duck & Abalone & the Pi Ba Tu Fu.
Would highly recommend the above few item, they are very well done.
The roast piglet is crispy and tasty, you don't have to order a whole piglet. They have half of it for small group like us (4pax)
Peking Duck is a must, crispy tasty skin, after that chop the meat out instead of fried rice if you really into meat. Or else you can use the duck meat for fried rice which is very good too.
Abalone with asparagus is nicely done, not tough yet tasty. 
Pi Ba Tu Fu is something different, not the usual TuFu taste. 
So, I can only say that when I am in Vietnam, I don't really try much of Viet Food but more on Chinese food. Coz is good, value for money !!

Good food poor service
Oct 2017 • Couples
We visited Tung Garden for dinner. Great ambience. We asked for prawns in drunken sauce and fried rice with roe and prawns. First thing we noticed was that while others were being offered wet towels we were not. We ordered for prawns with mango salad which was there in the menu but were later told that this was not available. Thirdly we asked for water and were given the costliest one in the menu without being asked which one we wanted. Fourthly had to wait for about 10 mins to get the bill. The rice was excellent, the best I have ever had, but this does not hide the fact that service levels are of abysmal standards at this place. Extremely poor experience..
